Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

The `getCorrelationPValues` method in the `PearsonsCorrelation` class calculates the p-values for the correlation matrix. It uses a t-distribution to compute the p-values based on the correlation coefficients. The calculation involves taking the absolute value of the correlation coefficient, computing the t-statistic, and then determining the p-value based on the t-distribution.

Given the nature of the failing test and the reported precision issue related to machine epsilon impacting p-values, the problem might lie in how machine epsilon is affecting the calculations within this method. The precision limitations imposed by machine epsilon could be causing the p-values to drop to 0 after reaching a certain threshold.

To address the precision limitation and prevent the p-values from dropping to 0 due to machine epsilon, adjustments may need to be made in the computation logic of the p-values within the `getCorrelationPValues` method of the `PearsonsCorrelation` class.

The likely fix would involve enhancing the precision handling in the p-value calculation process to ensure that the p-values remain accurate even with very small values.
